shortDescription: Stacks up to 7 playable z-levels (3 up / 3 down) into ONE banded RimWorld Map joined by synthetic RegionLink wormholes, so hauling/needs/work/storage come free from vanilla. Levels and per-level size are bought from a 146,000-cell budget; colder with altitude, richer ore and more cave with depth. Coast, river and lake tiles supported; Dubs Mint Minimap and Map Preview both patched. Rendering, interaction and generation all verified in play.
body:
# As above, So below II — V2

> V1 is **DELETED**. ~65 files / ~17,000 LOC.

## Pitch
Up to seven z-levels in ONE RimWorld `Map`. Priorities: (1) visual clarity from above, (2) performance, (3) vanilla parity.

> **QOL pass (five items) VERIFIED IN PLAY (run #172).** See §15.
> **§6b-LAKE is the one open visual defect** — and run #173 ELIMINATED the entire flow subsystem as its cause. Read §6b-LAKE before touching water.

---

# 1. ARCHITECTURE
One `Map`, size `(w, 1, bandCount × Slot)`; bands along **+z** from the deepest basement; permanently-fogged gutter between bands; `Slot = ceil((bandHeight+2)/64)×64` — **64-alignment is load-bearing**. Per-level sizes 126 / 190 / 254, each just under a 64 boundary.
**⚠ THE STACK IS EXTREMELY ANISOTROPIC: `Size.z / Size.x` is 2, 3, 4 … 7.** Any vanilla system that normalises by BOTH map dimensions is therefore silently distorted, and on an ordinary square map that class of bug can never appear. This is the suspected mechanism behind §6b-LAKE and is a standing thing to check first for any "it looks smeared/stretched" symptom.

### The one insight
`Region.Neighbors` is **topological, not spatial**. Wormhole `RegionLink`s between one-cell `RegionType.Portal` ends conduct connectivity without merging rooms/temperature/vacuum; `Reachability.CanReach` works **unpatched**. **But reachability ≠ a path** — 1.6's pathfinder is jobified and cannot traverse a synthetic link, hence segmented movement (§3).

### Hard 1.6 constraints
Path grid is an IJobParallelFor over EVERY cell ⇒ **total stacked cells is the runtime metric** · no `PathFinder.FindPath` · `BlocksDiagonalMovement` trips on unwalkable cells.

### ⚠ THE SLICING RULE — the recurring shape of every generation bug
The surface band is a horizontal SLICE of a tall map, so **anything vanilla anchors to the map's extent lands in the wrong band**. Five shapes now:
| Shape | Example | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **Anchor** — a point picked as a fraction of `Size.z` | river / lake centre (§6b); random/edge cell (§15a) | remap the point |
| **Field** — a gradient centred on the map centre | coastline (§6e) | re-centre the sample coordinate |
| **Noise space** — a slice ≠ a short map | Map Preview (§6d) | generate at full height, then crop |
| **Distance-to-extent** — a margin measured off `Size` | `CloseToEdge`, no-build edge (§15b/§15d) | re-base onto the cell's own band rect |
| **Aspect ratio** — a UV normalised by BOTH dims | `_MapSize` (§6b-LAKE, suspected) | ? — unproven, do not code yet |
**Classify a new bug into one of these five before theorising — but PROVE it, don't assume it.** Still unaudited: Basin, Cavern, Chasm, Cliffs, Hollow, Valley (all use `FalloffAtAngle`).

# 2. LEVEL PLAN — cell budget = **146,000**
`4 × 190 = 145,920` sets the figure; `2 × 254 = 130,048`, `7 × 126 = 112,896`; `5 × 190` and `7 × 190` refused.
`ABMapSizeLimit` owns it: `UpperLevels`/`LowerLevels` (0-3), `BandCount`, `SurfaceBand = lower`, `Fits`, `MaxSize`, `MaxLevelsFor`, `StackedCells`.
**Per-level size is SQUARE (`Size.x == bandHeight`)** — why `GenStep_Scatterer.CountFromPer10kCells` (which squares `Size.x`, not `map.Area`) already yields a per-BAND count. Only `GenStep_AnimaTrees` and `GenStep_TerrainPatches` read `map.Area`.
**⚠ THE LEVEL CHOOSER IS ALSO THE LAB.** `0 above / 0 below` generates an ORDINARY single-level map — the vanilla control for "is this even our bug". And because band count sets `Size.z`, the chooser is a **calibrated aspect-ratio dial**: 1 band = 1.0, 2 = 2.02, 4 = 4.04. Any symptom suspected of being ratio-driven can be measured, not argued.

### ⚠ THE CHOOSER UI — own the widget, don't patch the data
**`Dialog_AdvancedGameConfig.MapSizes` is `static readonly` and the reflection swap SILENTLY FAILED in play.** The postfix also re-snapped `GameInitData.mapSize` **every frame**. **Now:** our own radio buttons write `mapSize` directly. Window grown via an `InitialSize` postfix — **vanilla lays its columns from the top and never consults the height.**

# 3. CROSS-BAND MOVEMENT
Segmented at ONE interception: `StartPath` prefix → tick sweep → `Carry` re-issues `StartPath`. `ABWormhole.TryGetTransit` **BFSes the band graph**; hops must strictly decrease or pawns ping-pong.
**Caveat:** an intermediate level must be walkable between arrival and the next staircase. **STILL UNTESTED IN PLAY.**

# 4. GROUP ORDERING
**Correct:** `RecomputeDestinations` spreads the selection along the drag line, which between bands runs through the GUTTER. The odd/even signature ("3 and 5 fail, 2 and 4 don't") is the proof: only ODD counts sample exactly 0.5. Fix = normalise `start`/`end` into the commanded pawns' band. **Verified.**

# 5. ⚠ ONE DESCENT RULE — `ABBands.TryResolveVisibleBelow`
Descends while each level is see-through, stops at the first opaque floor or the bottom band. **NINE systems share it. SEVEN appearances of the single-`- Slot` bug. VERIFIED FIXED (#168).**
**Sun-shadow subtlety:** its mask is *neighbour*-based, so mask and descent are answered together by `TryResolveDropAround`, taking the **smallest** drop among the nine cells.
**Still single-band:** the realtime-things pass in `ABBelowDynamicDraw` (motes, fire).

# 6. SKY-MASS PRESENTATION — verified in play
**⚠ FOUR REJECTED ATTEMPTS:** force-linked wall masks · high-queue cover · wall-sprite suppression · theorising twice about "flat" mountains before running the below-layer report.
Despeckle (**wall dissolves only at 7+ open neighbours**) · one central fog hole · five-terrain plateau palette · cliff faces · alpine pass (**shallow-only tarns**, per-cell 6-cell edge rule, rim scree, exposure-thinned flora).
**Ore glyph bug:** ore defs have no `naturalTerrain` ⇒ a "can't happen" fallback drew the whole **atlas sheet** per cell.

# 6b. ⚠ WATER — `ABWaterV2.cs`. **1.6 water is a TWO-PASS SCREEN-SPACE effect**
`SectionLayer_Watergen` renders `waterDepthMaterial` into the **WaterDepth SUBCAMERA's** texture; the visible `Map/TerrainWater` material samples that (`_WaterOutputTex`) **at its own screen position**.
- **Water vanished from upper levels — VERIFIED FIXED (#171).** `SectionLayer_ABBelowWatergen` mirrors vanilla's `internal` Watergen and **overrides `DrawLayer` to target `SubcameraDefOf.WaterDepth.LayerId`**. Vanilla's Watergen is confirmed to be nothing but `SectionLayer_Terrain` + the depth material + that layer id — no per-vertex flow — so the mirror is faithful.
- **Rivers "did not generate" — VERIFIED FIXED (#167, re-confirmed #172).** Remap `GetRiverCenter` (not `Init`) preserving the *roll*; **`GetLakeCenter` needs the same patch or it undoes the first**.
- **The flow path is BAND-CORRECT.** `WaterInfo.SetTextures` builds `riverFlowTexture` at exactly `Size.x × Size.z` and publishes `_MapSize` as exactly those dims, so `worldPos.xz / _MapSize` is 1:1. Pixels are written **only** where `BaseTerrainAt(c).IsRiver`; only `TileMutatorWorker_River` ever writes `riverFlowMap`.

# 6b-LAKE. ⚠ **OPEN — water reads as streaking north-south. FLOW ELIMINATED BY MEASUREMENT (#173).**
### The measurement that settled it
Run #173 landed on a tile with **water but no water mutators**:
`lakeCenter invalid · riverGraph 0 · riverFlowMap NULL · riverFlowTexture null · band 0 water=580 baseRiver=0`
**The water streaked anyway.** There is no flow data in the process. Therefore the streaks are **not** river flow, **not** a ghost river, and **not** reachable from `riverFlowMap`. The ghost-river explanation is DEAD — do not revive it. Runs #172/#173 also killed the older "resolved as a side effect of the river fix" claim.
### What that leaves
With `riverFlowMap` null, `SetTextures` still calls `Shader.SetGlobalTexture(WaterOffsetTex, **null**)`, so the shader falls back to its declared default (white ⇒ a CONSTANT offset, not zero). A constant cannot make streaks. The only map-dependent input remaining is **`_MapSize = (190, 768)`**.
**HYPOTHESIS (unproven, no code written):** the water surface normalises its detail/reflection UV by `_MapSize`, so `u` spans `60/190` while `v` spans `60/768` — four times less variation vertically ⇒ features smear into north-south strands. `768/190 = 4.04`.
### ⚠ Why the §6b `_MapSize` rejection does NOT bind here
The rejected experiment changed **two** things: the global **and** a band-folded REPEAT-wrapped flow texture. The folded repeat texture is a sufficient independent explanation for the north-south flow it produced. **A map with no flow texture cannot exercise that mechanism**, so `_MapSize` can now be tested in isolation for the first time. This is a reason, not a loophole — anyone re-opening a documented rejection owes the same argument.
### The proof required before ANY code
Streak length must track `Size.z / Size.x` as a NUMBER, using the chooser as an aspect dial:
1. **0 up / 0 down** → ratio **1.00** → streaks absent, water isotropic. Also answers "is it vanilla" outright.
2. **1 up / 0 down** → ratio **2.02** → streaks **half** the current length.
Current observation is ratio 4.04. If the ordinary map streaks identically, it is vanilla 1.6 water and the investigation ends.
### If proven, the fix has a free first step
On a **riverless** map `riverFlowTexture` is null, so republishing `_MapSize` square breaks nothing — there is no flow lookup to damage. That fixes the riverless case in complete isolation and behind a bisect toggle, before anything is decided about the river case (which would need the flow texture rebuilt to match the new addressing).
### Vanilla fragility found, still unpatched
`TileMutatorWorker_River`'s flow builder ends `zero /= (float)num3` with **no guard for `num3 == 0`** ⇒ **NaN** into `riverFlowMap`; the texture is bilinear-filtered, so NaN bleeds. Irrelevant to the riverless case; relevant if the river case turns out to differ.

# 6c. DUBS MINT MINIMAP — active level only. **VERIFIED (#169)**
Reflection-only, **no foreign type in any signature**. Detection by **type presence**, not packageId.
**ONE RECT, NOT SEVEN PATCHES:** `height = view.height*Size.z/H`, `y = view.height*(H + bandMin - Size.z)/H`. **Culling is free.**
**Their texture blit cannot be reused:** `DrawTextureFitted` fits **preserving the TEXTURE's aspect** — the same anisotropy trap as §6b-LAKE, one layer up. Use `ScaleMode.StretchToFill`. `CameraDriver.CurrentRealPosition` is **private**; `Find.Camera.transform.position` is the same value.

# 6d. MAP PREVIEW — surface band only. **VERIFIED (#171)**
Map Preview never calls `MapGenerator.GenerateMap`, and a SLICE of position-based noise is a different map, not a slightly wrong one. **Fix = generate at full stacked height, show only the band's rows.** Most of it is NOT Harmony: `MaxMapSize`/`MapSizeOverride` are public static fields. `MaxMapSize.z` MUST rise (default 500; a stack reaches 896). Three patches: postfix `DetermineMapSize` (the CLAMPED entry point) gated to player-colony parents; postfix `MapPreviewResult.get_TexCoords` to crop; postfix `OnWorldTileSelected` to restate window width.
**`TryPendingSurfaceRect` falls back to a SIZE-INFERRED layout** so every generation-time patch behaves identically during a preview — including §15b's `CloseToEdge`.

# 6e. ⚠ COASTLINES — **VERIFIED (#171)**
`36100 water` out of exactly 36100 cells — **100%, and that precision was the diagnosis.**
**THE FALLOFF IS NOT SCALED WRONG, IT IS CENTRED WRONG.** `map.Size.z` appears in `FalloffAtAngle` in exactly ONE place: the final centring translate.
**Fix:** `z' = (z % Slot) + (map.Size.z - bandHeight) / 2`. **NO SCALING, deliberately.**
**ONE PATCH COVERS THE FAMILY:** nine coastal mutators, **none override `GetNoiseValue`**.

# 7. PER-LEVEL CHARACTER
Sky temp `-4°C × level` (compounds) · basement flat -6 · ore `×(1+0.45×(depth-1))`, cave openness `×(1+0.35×(depth-1))`, both AFTER the settings clamp.
**Snow line:** generation-time seeding **REMOVED** — vanilla melts per-CELL and the per-level offset already makes high levels cold.

# 8. CAMERA
`freeCameraPan` REMOVED. `ABCameraBounds.For(level)` keyed by **level**; **`maxZoom` left DERIVED**. **`panMargin` 63.5 now applies to EVERY level (§15c) — VERIFIED (#172).** Calibration dialog opens with the clamp UNLOCKED — **a calibration tool must suspend the limit it calibrates.**

# 9. ⚠ GENERATION COST
| Config | Tile | Cells | Carve | Things destroyed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 × 190 | — | 109,440 | 5.0 s | 14,971 |
| 7 × 126 | — | 112,896 | 30.4 s | 62,686 |
| 4 × 190 (#167) | **river** | 145,920 | 18.7 s | 56,318 |
| 4 × 190 (#168) | sparse | 145,920 | 2.5 s | 15,787 |
| 4 × 190 (#171) | **coast** | 145,920 | 15.2 s | 50,585 |
| 4 × 190 (#172) | lake+river+shrines | 145,920 | 3.1 s | 20,095 |
| 4 × 190 (#173) | bog, no mutators | 145,920 | **2.3 s** | 15,031 |
**#172/#173 confirm the §15b seam margin costs nothing measurable.**
**`Sky clear` is ~97% of the carve**; **`0 rocks spawned`**.
**⚠ THE REAL DRIVER IS BIOME CONTENT, NOT CELL COUNT** — 9× spread at identical size. **Any carve timing MUST record the tile.**
**THE FIX — extend the doomed-band genstep skip** (precedent: `Patch_WildPlantSpawner_ABSkipDoomedBands`, 16.9 s → 4.2 s).
**HARD CONSTRAINT: per-cell gensteps scope safely; `map.Area`-count scatterers do NOT** (but the scatterer family counts off `Size.x²`, so it is safe). **Do not blanket-skip the water/coast mutators.**

# 10. RUNTIME PERF — 59.6 fps @96 pawns, mod ≈2% frame.

# 11. VERTICAL LINKS — elevator SHIPPED, **untested**.

# 12. DIAGNOSTICS
band info · below layer report · below pawn report · **water report** · transit health · stuck probe · lighting/shader/biome reports · bisect toggles · ABGenProfile · camera calibration.
**The water report earned its keep at #173** — four lines (`riverGraph 0 / riverFlowMap NULL / riverFlowTexture null / baseRiver=0`) plus one screenshot eliminated an entire subsystem that two investigations had been searching.
**⚠ The bisect toggles PERSIST in the pinned palette across runs** — #172 opened with `belowWater=False` from an earlier session, which would have looked exactly like the §6b regression. **Read the bisect line before trusting any water observation.**
**The start-spot failure log is a first-class diagnostic.**

# 13. OPEN WORK
1. **§6b-LAKE** — two aspect-ratio controls outstanding (1.00 and 2.02). **Do NOT write code before they land.**
2. **Doomed-band genstep scoping pass** (§9) — band 1 first, and record the tile.
3. **Audit the other `FalloffAtAngle` mutators** — Basin, Cavern, Chasm, Cliffs, Hollow, Valley.
4. **Never exercised in play:** multi-hop stair router, elevator, reload fix. **Basement paths still untested** — #172/#173 were both 3-up/0-down, so `surfaceBand=0` and band-folded addressing has never run.
5. Realtime-things pass still single-band.
6. Selection bracket **drifts upward as you zoom out**.
7. **Option E — waterfalls**: de-risked by §6b.
8. COMBAT never verified · vertical conduit · compat audit · **store page still says three levels**.

# 14. LESSONS (telegraphic)
**Run the diagnostic before the third theory** — #173 nearly broke it again: four theories about streaks before conceding no data existed · **PROVE A SUBSYSTEM INNOCENT AS HARD AS YOU'D PROVE IT GUILTY** — the single most valuable move of #173 was finding a map with ZERO flow data; the symptom survived and an entire subsystem died with one screenshot · **THE BEST CONTROL IS A MAP WHERE THE SUSPECT CANNOT EXIST** — don't measure the suspect, remove it · **a documented rejection may be re-opened, but only by naming the CONFOUND that invalidates it** — the `_MapSize` rejection bundled a folded flow texture, and a riverless map cannot exercise that · **"resolved as a side effect" is NOT resolved** · **build the A/B discriminator INTO any change whose mechanism you cannot read** · **a beautiful fit is not evidence** · **an EXACT number is a diagnosis** — demand the symptom track a ratio before coding · **the level chooser is a calibrated aspect dial; use the product's own knobs as lab equipment** · **the ABSENCE of a known error line is a valid pass signal** · **a UNIFORM symptom is a scale/constant, a PATCHY one is data** · **A STACKED MAP IS 2-7× ANISOTROPIC — suspect anything normalised by BOTH map dimensions** · **poll the monitor even when nothing auto-prompts** · **when N call sites share ONE linear mapping, re-aim the shared parameter** · **find the ONE virtual everything funnels through** — nine coastal mutators / every scatterer's `CanScatterAt` / one `CloseToEdge` · **read the foreign mod's OWN compat classes first** · **never put a foreign type in a patch-class signature** · **re-centre, don't rescale** · **not every water bug is the slicing rule — check before assuming** · **position-based noise means a SLICE of a tall map ≠ a short map** · **an odd/even or count-dependent symptom is arithmetic** · **when a symptom says "X is missing", ask how many PASSES X takes** · **two runs of the same config are only comparable if the TILE matches** · **grep every `- Slot`** · **patch the method that PRODUCES a value, not the one that stores it** · **own the widget instead of patching the data it reads** · **ALTITUDE IS DRAW ORDER — check where a new overlay sorts against `WorldClipper`** · **`Banded` is FALSE for the whole of map generation** · **vanilla divides by a count without guarding zero — NaN in a bilinear texture bleeds** · **a null global texture falls back to the SHADER'S default, which is not necessarily zero** · ore defs have no naturalTerrain · a `Graphic_Linked` base material is the whole ATLAS SHEET · **"can't happen" fallbacks are what the player photographs** · enforce spatial rules PER CELL · **balance GUI clip/group pops in a `finally`** · statics keyed by game-scoped ids leak — CWT · **Unity textures are not GC'd with their owner** · **any type with a `Material` field needs `[StaticConstructorOnStartup]`** · never cache comps while Scribe active · FinalizeInit = worker thread · `SectionLayer` subclasses are **auto-discovered**.

# 15. QOL PASS — five items. **ALL VERIFIED IN PLAY (run #172)**

## 15a. Nothing may exist in the void — `ABBandSafety.cs`
Pawns were spawning in the GUTTER, where there is no region: they cannot path, be reached, or be rescued by any ordinary mechanism.
**Three layers, deliberately redundant:** the **finders** (`RandomEdgeCell(Rot4,Map)`, the 5-arg `TryFindRandomEdgeCellWith`, `RandomCell`) now answer inside the SURFACE band; a prefix on the **7-arg `GenSpawn.Spawn`** (every overload funnels into it) rewrites `loc` before vanilla reads it; and a **120-tick sweep** using `Position` + `Notify_Teleported` catches teleports, psycasts, foreign spawners and pre-fix saves.
**Relocation is ALWAYS to the surface**, by decision: a spawn that landed in the void has proven its chooser does not understand bands, so the nearest band is an accident of which seam it fell into, not evidence of intent.
Scoped to Pawns and to the GUTTER only. Inert during generation (`Banded` is false there); that window has `RescueStrandedColonists`.

## 15b. Structures must not straddle a seam — `CloseToEdge`, re-based
**Root cause is the slicing rule's distance-to-extent shape.** `GenGrid.CloseToEdge` measures against `map.Size`, so on a stack the only "edges" are the deepest basement's floor and the top of the sky: **the surface band reported itself as inland everywhere, including the rows that butt onto a seam.** Every generator's edge declaration was silently void.
**One prefix re-bases the distance onto the cell's OWN band rect** (live via `ABBands`, mid-generation via `TryPendingSurfaceRect`). Eleven call sites, all cold, all inherit the fix using their own numbers.
**Backstop:** a postfix on `GenStep_Scatterer.CanScatterAt` rejects cells within 10 of a band's Z seam. Z only. Postfixing the base reaches the whole family because every stock override opens with `if (!base.CanScatterAt(...)) return false;`.

## 15c. Camera bounds — one row for every level
`For` gave `panMargin` 63.5 to levels +1..+3 and 0 to the surface and below, purely because calibration had only been run in the sky — so the ground floor, where nearly all play happens, was the one level whose framing felt broken. **There was never a per-level reason:** `panMargin` is framing only, and the view clip guarantees overhang shows curtain. Now uniform.

## 15d. Vanilla's no-build map edge — REMOVED on banded maps. `ABNoBuildEdge.cs`
Both halves were anchored to the stack: the 10-cell strip landed on the deepest basement's floor and the top of the sky and nowhere else, and `DrawMapEdgeLines` boxed the whole 190×768 stack.
Removed rather than re-based — **per-band is one flag away** (`ABNoBuildEdge.Removed`), because 15b already re-bases the underlying test.
**Stated consequence:** vanilla's strip is also what stops a colony sealing its map edge and starving the pawn-entry finder.
The no-**zone** rule is KEPT (per-band for free via 15b); only its whole-stack overlay box is suppressed.

## 15e. Drop pods fall through the levels — `ABSkyfallerRelay.cs`
**Two faults, one symptom:** (1) **the curtain ate the flight** — a skyfaller's `DrawPos` starts tens of cells north of its target, so most of the descent is drawn outside its own band, and `AltitudeLayer.WorldClipper` sorts **above** `AltitudeLayer.Skyfaller`. Nothing was broken; it was painted over. (2) **a pod bound elsewhere was culled** by the band-clipped view rect.
**One mechanism for both:** suppress vanilla's draw (prefix on `Skyfaller.DrawAt` — reached only by skyfallers, unlike `Thing.DynamicDrawPhaseAt`) and re-issue once via `DrawNowAt`, translated by `(viewedBand - itsBand) * Slot`. Suppressing the whole body parks the drop-spot shadow too, which is correct: the relay's call re-runs it, so the shadow draws once at the real landing cell.
**Altitude is chosen PER FRAME:** normal while over its own level, lifted above `WorldClipper` only while out over the curtain. Lifting unconditionally would render every landing at full brightness through the night lighting overlay — visible only after dark.
**Pass-through timing:** shown for all but the last `levelsAbove × 18` ticks; outgoing (`reversed`) mirrors off `ageTicks`. `levelsAbove == 0` reduces exactly to vanilla.
`Skyfaller_FlyingPawn` excluded — it OVERRIDES `DrawAt`, so suppression never fires for it and relaying would double-draw.

## TESTING RULE
`isolated=true`. **Compat tests need the target mod as a companion** — Dubs (`dubwise.dubsmintminimap`) and Map Preview (`m00nl1ght.MapPreview`) are both INACTIVE in the user's real list. Multi-level tests need `quicktest=false`. **Water tests need the right tile — and #173 proves a tile with NO water mutators is sometimes the most valuable one.** Note the tile in any perf comparison. **A `surfaceBand=0` config cannot exercise band-folded addressing.**
**Check the bisect line before trusting a water observation** — the toggles persist across runs.
